newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lockheed no comment on Zodiac purchase talk.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed no comment on Zodiac purchase talk.

text.p: U.S. aerospace giant Lockheed Martin declined to comment on Friday on rumours it was in talks to buy French aircraft equipment company Zodiac SA.
"Lockheed Martin does not speculate on any rumours," a spokeswoman for the company said in Paris.

A Zodiac spokesman earlier denied a report in magazine La Vie Francaise that said it was in talks for Lockheed to buy Zodiac. The spokesman said, "I can only repeat that we deny there are any plans to change the ownership."
Shares in Zodiac were up three percent at 1,447 francs on market talk spurred by the report, traders said.

The magazine report said the acquisition talks on Lockheed's side were led by the British branch of Rothschild bank and Societe Generale for the French company, with a friendly offer in view. Zodiac chairman Jean-Louis Gerondeau would retain his post, the report said.

Lockheed Martin posted 1995 revenues of $22.85 billion and is the world's biggest defence contractor. Its interests span combat planes, space and missiles. Its latest major U.S. acquisition is defence electronics specialist Loral Corp.

Zodiac had 1995/96 sales of 3.4 billion francs. It has not published profit figures for the year but posted 1994/95 net profit before goodwill amortisation of 174 million francs, the Zodiac spokesman said.
The magazine report said Zodiac's market capitalisation was 6.85 billion francs, or two times turnover while other French companies in the sector traded at one times turnover.
